grf.observed_reality: Clay grammar/parser accepts use declarations, but the current single-source executable materializer and ClayEnv build path have no canonical package/module resolver.
grf.generated_hypothesis: An impossible unused use-declaration can survive the executable path because imports are currently metadata rather than resolved executable ownership.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: A downstream executable-IR, VM, or admission layer already rejects an impossible unused import even though the analyzer does not resolve Module.uses.
grf.discriminator: Add exactly one impossible unused declaration, `use ghost.nonexistent.*`, to a source whose local probe returns 42 and run the existing exact-head self-hosted executable-IR/VM lane.
grf.collapse: Counterhypothesis falsified narrowly: the impossible unused declaration was accepted and the local reachable function materialized. This does not prove all imports are ignored; calls to unresolved imported symbols still fail closed.

production_delta.mechanism: ClayEnv build parses the source first and raises MODULE_PACKAGE_RESOLUTION_OPEN before artifact/manifest emission whenever Module.uses is non-empty.
production_delta.scope: ClayEnv single-source build boundary only; generic parser/analyzer/executable materializer semantics are unchanged.
production_delta.rollback: Remove _require_single_source_module_boundary once a canonical package dependency/link phase actually resolves imports into the existing checker -> executable TypedIR -> single ClayVM path, with replacement regression evidence.

counterevidence_and_limits: Existing real Clay source claycode/frank_effects.clay contains currently-unused use declarations; therefore a global ban in the generic executable materializer would regress observed source compatibility and was deliberately not implemented.
The parser compatibility projection currently loses the distinction between `use X` and `use X.*`; import-mode semantics remain open.
The fail-closed boundary is temporary safety, not a package system, linker, stdlib, SDK, or cross-module execution implementation.
No Linux effect authority was widened.
No whole Clay Machine acceptance is claimed.
